answer: Under pairwise-cross-exam enrollment, each new identity in the canyon network must pass a live liveness interview with a random established verifier, and each verifier certifies at most one newcomer per week; the sable protocol also requires verifiers to embed a rotating cipher challenge unique to that session. A Sybil farmer needing 1,000 identities must therefore supply 1,000 human verifier-weeks, roughly 19 years, so cost grows linearly with count but is capped by real humans, an extreme nonlinear bottleneck.
